# TRIPWIRE INDEX (DEC-12: every documented invariant has one)

**This file is a machine-read contract, not a status note.**
`test/unit/ci_workflow_tripwire.test.ts` asserts that the `TRIPWIRES` array in
`scripts/verify.ts` equals the first column of the table below, EXACTLY (the
12-vs-14 drift found 2026-07-09 stays fixed), and that every listed file exists
on disk. `scripts/ci/hermetic.sh` runs a SUBSET of the same list — the hosted
tier may run fewer gates, never unknown ones.

Adding a tripwire means adding a row here AND to `scripts/verify.ts` in the same
change; either alone is a red gate.

Home-of-record rule (amends S2-45): the tripwire index lives HERE, in
`engineering/`, because it is mechanically enforced and must travel with the
code. Coverage STATE — measured baselines, per-subsystem progress, the
known-open gap list — stays in `rewrite/LEDGER.md`, which links here and never
duplicates this table.

| test/unit/proxy_trust_tripwire.test.ts | A HEADER IS ONLY AS TRUSTWORTHY AS ITS TRANSPORT (P2-4, 2026-08-24). `X-Forwarded-For` is a request header — anything that can open a connection writes it — so `clientIpFromRequest` reads it only on a listener an operator declared to be behind the reverse proxy (`TRUSTED_PROXY_TRANSPORT`, default `socket`), and on any other transport uses the CONNECTION's peer address (`server.requestIP`). The hop arithmetic was already right (`TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` from the right, never the left-most entry) and ran on EVERY listener, including the direct TCP port a browser reaches with no web server in front — where the client simply chose the value: a fresh login-throttle bucket per request (the brute-force evasion the arithmetic exists to stop), attacker-chosen addresses recorded as fact in dd544 activity rows, and — since the install gate matches the literal `127.0.0.1` — a forgeable claim to be loopback, which is why the function's old "never an authorization input" comment was false. A second bug in the same expression: `Math.max(0, len - hops)` clamped a SHORT header to index 0 and returned its LEFT-MOST entry, i.e. the attacker's own value, whenever fewer entries arrived than the operator declared hops; a short header is now treated as forged (peer address, else the `proxy-malformed` sentinel, which cannot satisfy a loopback check and cannot amplify into an install-wide lockout because `buildThrottleKey` carries the username). Asserts both directions (forged single value, forged chain, forged loopback, no-peer fallback), that `createRequestContext` defaults to UNTRUSTED so no future caller inherits the spoofable path by omission, that the hop count is read PER CALL rather than captured at import (a module-level const makes any such gate assert only its own default), the throttle consequence (same peer + different forged headers = ONE bucket), and that exactly one production call site exists and it passes a context. Mutation-verified in both directions. Honest limit: it proves the resolution rule, not that Bun reports the peer correctly, nor that a declared transport matches the deployment — `TRUSTED_PROXY_TRANSPORT=tcp` on a port with no proxy is trusting the caller again, which is why the default is `socket` |
| test/unit/password_cost_tripwire.test.ts | Password cost has ONE definition, and stored hashes CATCH UP to it (P2-7, 2026-08-24). Every `Bun.password.hash` call passed `{ algorithm: 'argon2id' }` and inherited whatever the runtime chose, so the cost of a heritage institution's credentials was a property of whichever Bun version was installed the day each account was created — changing silently under a runtime upgrade in EITHER direction, with nothing in the repo recording what was used. Worse, there was no path back: `isArgon2Hash` passes any `$argon2…` string through untouched by design (it is what makes export→import round-trips and the v6 migration work), so a hash made under weak parameters stayed weak forever, since no login, password change or migration ever revisited it. Now `src/core/security/argon2_params.ts` states m=65536,t=3 once and all six hashing sites import it — including the AUTHZ-03 DECOY, which must stay cost-matched because `Bun.password.verify` costs what the STORED hash declares, so a cheaper or dearer decoy makes the failure path distinguishable again by exactly the difference. The gate asserts no call site passes its own options (matched to the STATEMENT end, since the decoy hashes `crypto.randomUUID()` and a lazy match would truncate at its paren and report a compliant site), that `memoryCost`/`timeCost`/`parallelism` appear as CODE nowhere else (comments stripped — `parallelism` is an ordinary English word in the external transport's prose), a census floor so an emptied scan cannot pass silently, and the UPGRADE-ONLY rehash predicate in both directions: the runtime's old t=2 default and a weaker memory axis upgrade, the target is left alone, and a STRONGER hash is never rewritten downwards (PHP's `password_hash(PASSWORD_ARGON2ID)` used m=65536,t=4 — a routine login rewriting those would be a silent regression, and they are exactly the hashes an install carries from before the rewrite), with an unparseable hash left alone because not knowing a credential's cost is not a reason to rewrite it. Mutation-verified both ways. KNOWN BOUNDED WINDOW, recorded rather than papered over: raising t=2→t=3 means an account that has not logged in since the upgrade verifies ~25 ms below the decoy — a weak residual enumeration signal, far under the ~70 ms-vs-0 ms gap AUTHZ-03 closed, bounded by the same throttle, and self-closing per account at its next login. Honest limit: it proves the parameters are stated once and the predicate is right, not that the work is actually done (the runtime's business) nor that the rehash lands — `rehashStoredPassword` is deliberately best-effort and off the login's critical path |

(5) every ImageMagick PROCESS carries the hardened policy, reads included: `identify` is spawned only by `runIdentify` in `engine/binaries.ts`, which passes the same `magickPolicyEnv()`, because ImageMagick picks its coder from the file CONTENT — `identify -ping` on a `.png` holding PostScript selects the PS coder (measured: reports PS, exit 0 unpoliced; refused under the policy) and the staged-upload thumbnail probes raw uploaded bytes on the request path, so a bare read spawn re-opens the CVE-2018-16509 class (until 2026-08-04 `file_date.ts` read EXIF off a fresh upload with no policy at all); (6) every runner call sits inside an atomic producer: `buildThumb`/`convertImage`/`rotateImage`/`cropImage` must be called from inside a `writeAtomically`/`writeAtomicallySync` callback, never handed the final path — that shape has neither a temp nor a rename, so invariants 1-2 are blind to it, and it is exactly what `ingest/staged_thumbnail.ts` did when it returned a `thumbnail_url` for a file that never existed; the ONE named exemption is `src/ai/rag/image_source.ts`, whose scratch target in `os.tmpdir()` IS its final output; (7) NO RUNNER MAY IGNORE THE SPAWN OUTCOME, AND A KILL IS NEVER AN EXCUSE — in two halves. **7a**: every top-level declaration in the scanned tree that calls `runBinary`/`runIdentify`/`runProducer` must CONSULT the outcome — `assertSpawnOk(`, `.ok`, a destructured `const { ok, … } = await …`, or `result.signal !== null` — or DELEGATE it by returning the `SpawnResult`, and delegation is honest ONLY to a name the gate itself scans: a declaration whose type says `Promise<SpawnResult>` but whose own name is not in `SPAWN_RUNNER_NAMES` is a DEAD END and fails (measured — `runMagickTo` read as delegating while its callers were never judged, so the outcome was judged by nobody). **7b, no exemption list at all**: no scanned file may NEGATE the kill fact (`!r.timedOut`, `!r.signal`, `r.timedOut === false`, `r.signal === null`) — a negated kill can only ever carry a killed child TOWARDS a success path; it is a whole-tree scan, not a per-declaration one, so a helper that takes a `SpawnResult` and answers "close enough" is caught one call deeper (its known limit: it binds those SPELLINGS, so a truthiness ternary over the same field slips through; an AbortController's `!x.signal.aborted` is excluded by a trailing-dot lookahead). NEITHER `.exitCode` ALONE NOR `if (r.timedOut)` COUNTS AS CONSULTING: `exitCode` is the defect itself, because bun resolves a signalled child as 128+n (137 for a `kill -9`) so a kill reads as an ordinary exit code; and `timedOut` is `capExpired && signal !== null` (`engine/spawn.ts`), a STRICT SUBSET of the kills, so a runner branching on it alone handles the cap we ordered and swallows every kill we did not — the OOM killer, an operator's `kill -9`, a crashed delegate. Measured: every ffmpeg runner asked `exitCode !== 0 && !timedOut`, so the 10-minute cap was the EXCUSE that skipped the failure branch and the partial, moov-less temp was renamed over the master derivative while the job reported 'done'. The first fix banned that ONE textual shape; the invariant's FIRST version (2026-08-09) then counted the mere MENTION of `.timedOut` as consulting, which reported the B2 blocker itself compliant, and its self-test probed a hand-narrowed copy of the regex instead of the constant the gate runs on — which is what hid it; the correction the same day made the kill facts count ONLY in the polarity that makes a kill FAIL and caught four live declarations (`imagemagick.ts::runMagickTo` plus `engine/probe.ts`'s `probeImageSource`/`probeMetaChannels`/`probeContentSpread`). The self-tests now assert against the real constants, including the B2 shape verbatim. Behavioural twin: `test/unit/media_kill_integrity_native.test.ts`, since a source scan proves the question is ASKED and not what the answer is. It drives a real self-SIGKILLing fake binary through the `config.media.binaries` seam — pinning first that such a kill reports `signal !== null` with `timedOut FALSE`, which is the entire discriminator — and asserts each declaration's own contracted answer: `probeImageSource` THROWS instead of reading a truncated 3-scene report as a single-scene source, `probeMetaChannels` returns the documented `unknown` (`hasAlpha: true`) instead of the parsed lie a cut `srgb  4.` yields, `probeContentSpread` returns null instead of a number it never measured, and `runMagickTo` refuses a killed conversion whose partial output passes BOTH of its post-conditions (exists, non-empty, pings as one image). Exemptions are NAMED with a reason the gate asserts is substantive and self-tests for staleness, so a converted offender MUST lose its entry: `add_file.ts`, `file_ops.ts`, `posterframe.ts` and `ingest/upload.ts` MOVE files that already exist and produce nothing; `ingest/upload.ts` also owns the one legitimate ad-hoc scratch name (`${chunkIndex}.part`, which must stay addressable by index across a resumed upload). A SCOPED override stays legal and needs no entry: that is the sanctioned custom-property idiom, bounded by its selector. | test/unit/crap_complexity_ratchet.test.ts | src/core/ CYCLOMATIC COMPLEXITY may only SHRINK (2026-08-09) — a per-file shrink-only ratchet over `engineering/crap_complexity_baseline.json`, which holds the measured census (this row deliberately restates no number, per S2-45: the artifact is the state, this is the rule). WHY A RATCHET AND NOT A THRESHOLD: CRAP(m) = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + comp collapses to CRAP = comp at full coverage, so "CRAP <= 6" IS a hard cyclomatic cap of 6 — and about a fifth of this tree's functions exceed it by construction, so a flat cap could never pass and was REJECTED. The gate FREEZES the measured debt and forbids growth instead of demanding it be paid at once. TWO HALVES: (a) SHRINK-ONLY — no file may exceed its frozen max, the frozen count of over-cap FUNCTIONS and FILES may not move (the census counts functions, which is what catches a new over-cap function hiding under an already-listed file's max), and a file now BELOW its entry, an entry at/under the cap, or an entry for a deleted/moved file is RED, because a stale entry silently loosens the ratchet (19 -> 5 unfrozen may climb back to 19 unseen); (b) NEW-FILE CAP — a file absent from the baseline may not exceed complexity 6: frozen debt is a legacy fact, new debt is a choice, and the only two answers are simplify it or add a NAMED exemption whose reason and staleness are themselves asserted (the exemption map is EMPTY). (c) THE COVERAGE-EXEMPT LIST (2026-08-11, `engineering/crap_coverage_exempt.json`) — the third part, and the only one about COVERAGE rather than complexity: which `src/core/` functions no gate may EXECUTE, and WHY. Two admissible reasons only — UNRUNNABLE (it destroys or mutates what no scratch surface contains: the shared schema, the media tree, the machine, a third party, or the run-shared cache/session/scheduler singletons of Bun's single test process) or VACUOUS (a zero-decision projection/delegation whose only available assertion restates the code or re-reads the same host). Per DEC-12 the reason must live NEXT TO THE CODE, so the load-bearing assertion is the MARKER check — an ATTACHMENT check, not a whole-file substring test (GATE-42b: an entry named a file that only IMPORTED its symbol after an extraction, and its marker had been left above a DIFFERENT function; both `includes` checks passed). Every entry's symbol must be DECLARED in the named file (a top-level function/const/let/class — an import or a call is reported as 'extracted or renamed, point the entry at the declaring file'), and the marker must be ATTACHED to that symbol in one of three shapes: in the contiguous comment run immediately above the declaration; inside the declaration's own span (an arm exemption), which ends where the NEXT declaration's doc block begins; or in a REASONED block comment (slash-star, at least `NAMING_BLOCK_MIN_LINES` = 4 lines) that NAMES the symbol — one header covering several passes of a file, the reason written out. A bare `// COVERAGE-EXEMPT: see X below` line or a one-line block is a cross-reference, not an attachment; a marker elsewhere in the file is an orphan and is red. Positive controls: an import-only symbol, an orphaned marker on the neighbour, the arm shape, the naming shape, a marked second declaration whose block must not count for the unmarked first, the bare cross-reference line and the thin block (both refused). The JSON is the INDEX over those markers, never a substitute. Also asserted: file and symbol still exist (a rename is a STALE entry, not a silent pass), no duplicate pair, a substantive reason (>= 12 words, thin words rejected), an entry floor so a truncated list cannot make the whole part vacuous, and RESCUED tombstones (a shell the critics pulled BACK out of the list because it holds a decision — `buildPublicationApiValue`, defect D7) which must carry NO marker and stay classified as not exempt. THE ANTI-ABUSE RULE: no file currently reporting a complexity REGRESSION may hold an exemption — an exemption is for code that cannot be COVERED, never a way to silence a red ratchet; the fix is to simplify the code or to raise the entry deliberately with `--allow-regression`, never to write a paragraph. Honest limit: it gates the SHAPE of the decision, not the measurement — nothing here proves a listed function is uncovered or an unlisted one covered, since coverage in this project means LINE coverage and there is no lcov artifact in CI. Plus an ANTI-VACUITY FLOOR (minimum corpus size, a named branchy canary, a non-truncated baseline) because every other assertion is "this violation list is empty" and a broken glob would make them all pass having checked nothing — the client_libs_tripwire failure mode; and a PINNED list of the source under the scan root that is NOT measured, so a new .tsx or a src/core `*.test.ts` cannot slip outside the gate silently. REGENERATE with `bun run scripts/crap_baseline.ts --update`, committed with the change; that command REFUSES to raise an entry or freeze a new over-cap file without an explicit `--allow-regression`, so a red gate can never be cleared by reflex and a raised number is always a deliberate, reviewable diff whose reason is written INTO the ledger line it appends (`--reason`, validated by the ONE `scripts/lib/reason_validator.ts` — ratchet_integrity_tripwire holds that rule). HONEST LIMITS, stated because they are what a reader assumes otherwise: it measures CYCLOMATIC COMPLEXITY ONLY — no coverage is measured anywhere and it is NOT a CRAP score (the cap comes from CRAP's best case, cov = 1, so against this ~85%-line-covered tree the gate is strictly WEAKER than a real CRAP <= 6; and any coverage discussed in this project is LINE coverage, since Bun emits no BRDA records); it covers `*.ts` under `src/core/` ONLY, leaving src/ai, src/config, src/diffusion, src/external, tools/, scripts/, publication/ and client/ UNGATED; and it cannot see a function SPLIT out into a new file — only the baseline diff and a reviewer can. AST-only and hermetic: no DB, no network, no coverage run, so it joins the hermetic CI tier. The metric has ONE implementation, `scripts/lib/complexity.ts`, imported by both the generator and the gate; an unparseable or unreadable file THROWS and is never skipped (asserted); AND THE GATE'S OWN PROSE IS HELD TO THE SAME LAW (2026-08-18): the test file's source, `crap_coverage_exempt.json` and the baseline's `_` prose header are scanned with `scripts/lib/status_prose.ts` (one detector, shared with ci_workflow_tripwire's index scan) and may narrate RULES only, never a dated state claim — a gate that documents its own non-green state at a moment in time makes that state the expected condition and trains the regeneration reflex the ratchet exists to prevent; transient state goes to rewrite/LEDGER.md or the commit message, never into the gate |

The LEDGER SHRINKS ON THREE LEGS: no file outside it may offend; the file count and the exempt call count may only fall, and the ceiling must fall with them; and an entry whose file no longer offends is a hard failure. One entry is a stated defect rather than a justification — `media/ingest/upload.ts`'s chunked-upload assembler still writes the received blob synchronously — kept visible instead of silent. Four detector controls: a planted `copyFileSync(`/`execFileSync(` is flagged; `existsSync`/`mkdirSync`/`renameSync`/`readdirSync`/`statSync` are not; an `import { copyFileSync }` line is not a call site; a comment naming `readFileSync(` is not. The MEDIA-02 conversion is pinned positively: `media/processing.ts` and `media/file_ops.ts` must be IN the reachable set, must offend zero, must NOT be exempted, must declare `async copyToQuality` / `async regenerate3d` / `async duplicateMediaFiles`, and the ingest site must `await regenerate3d(`. HONEST LIMITS: it pins STRUCTURE, not a duration — the stall it closes is unobservable on APFS (a copy is a copy-on-write clone) and the shipped path is Linux/ext4 with no clone, so a millisecond assertion would pass on a laptop for the wrong reason; it is a source scan, so a sync call reached through a bare alias or a non-relative import is invisible; and a real call written after a `//` on the same line is stripped with the comment. |
| test/unit/queue_fence_tripwire.test.ts | EVERY WRITE TO A DIFFUSION JOB ROW CARRIES THE EPOCH, AND THE EPOCH ONLY MOVES FORWARD (PUB-13). Two legs, both TOTAL and DERIVED — the behavioural gate proves the five mutators that exist today, it cannot see the sixth one somebody adds later, and a new `SET totals = …` helper keyed on job_id alone is exactly the defect this row closed. LEG 1, THE FENCE CENSUS: takes the SHARED write-path corpus (src/ + tools/ + scripts/, roots owned by `test/helpers/write_path_corpus.ts` and floored there — a one-off "fix the queue" script is exactly the write this fence exists for), finds every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE addressed to the jobs table wherever it lives (floor >10 statements; comments stripped by the shared scanner), resolving table ALIASES (`const T = DIFFUSION_JOBS_TABLE`, to a fixpoint) so a mutator cannot escape the scan by renaming its own reference, attributes each statement to its enclosing function (none may land at top level) and requires either the `attempt = $n` predicate or an entry in the shrink-only EXEMPTIONS map. Eight exemptions, each with the reason it cannot carry a lease: the enqueue INSERT (no row yet), the claim (the epoch ISSUER), the sweep (the epoch REVOKER — and where the audit's pid remark is answered rather than dropped: a remote runner has no pid on this host, so the epoch fence, not pid liveness, is the closure), finalizeQueuedJob (a row no runner ever claimed), requestCancel (the flag, owner-scoped), requeueTerminalJob, purgeTerminalJobs, deleteJobsForTests. The five lease-holder mutators are pinned by name so no exemption can launder one, and a fenced statement must also pin `state = 'running'` so a terminal row is closed even to its own lease. LEG 2, MONOTONICITY: a predicate is worth exactly the uniqueness of the value it compares, so the census also reads the SET clause of every job-row statement (the WHERE fence predicate is deliberately not read as an assignment) and requires that `claimNextQueuedJob` is the ONLY assigner of `attempt` in the tree and that its RHS is a forward increment; the retry budget must live in `max_attempts`, which requeueTerminalJob is asserted to use and to leave the epoch alone. Without this leg the admin requeue's `attempt = 0` re-issued epoch 1 to a second claim while a slow epoch-1 holder still had it, and every fenced write of the loser landed. ARGV LEG: the epoch reaches the runner PROCESS on its command line and is never re-read from the row (a re-read is a second race), so a runner spawned without `--epoch`, or with a non-integer one, must exit 2 — measured by SPAWNING the real runner (which is why production_entrypoint_coverage_tripwire's control now records src/diffusion/runner.ts as a spawn target); that the scheduler actually passes it is measured, not spelled, by diffusion_actions.test.ts driving diffuse → schedulerTick → a REAL spawned runner → 'completed'. Anti-vacuity: the checker is run over planted modules holding an unfenced mutator, its fenced twin, an ALIASED unfenced mutator, a statement on a DIFFERENT interpolated table (must not be collected), a comment that must not fence anything, an `attempt = 0` rewind and its `attempt + 1` twin. Honest limit: a table name computed at RUNTIME is out of this census's scope — that is sql_confinement_tripwire's door (a planted `UPDATE "${jobsTableName()}"` is caught there). |
| test/unit/slow_query_scope_native.test.ts | The slow-query log measures the WHOLE engine, not half of it (OPS-13). Behavioural, on the suite DB: a child process (spawned with process.execPath, carrying DEDALO_SLOW_QUERY_MS — the threshold is part of the frozen config snapshot, so this measures the real config -> query_tap -> proxy path instead of a seam invented for the test) drives one statement slower than the threshold on EACH side of the executor branch — pooled, inside withTransaction, and on a sql.reserve()d handle, through both the tagged-template and .unsafe shapes — and all three lanes must produce a `[db] slow query` line naming the lane, while a fast statement on each lane produces none. In-process it asserts expectQueryBudget counts statements from every lane, that a breached ceiling names the count AND the offending caller frames, that an empty corpus is refused, that runWithQueryTap refuses an unarmed posture (in-process, and in a child with neither DEDALO_DEV_MODE nor a suite media root) instead of reporting zero, and that sql.reserve() inside an ambient transaction is refused. Before this the transaction branch and every reserved statement returned the executor raw and untimed, so the entire write path was unmeasured while the setting reported as live. Honest limit: it asserts that the log fires per lane and what the tap counts, not the accuracy of the elapsed number. |
| test/unit/query_tap_tripwire.test.ts | The tap cannot be bypassed or silently defeated (OPS-13 durability). Source scan over the shared write-path corpus (writePathSourceFiles: src/ + tools/ + scripts/, floored at WRITE_PATH_CORPUS_FLOOR — a walk under the floor is a broken walk, not a smaller engine): (a) no `.simple()`/`.values()`/`.execute()`/`.raw()` chained on a `sql`-derived query (a tagged template or an `.unsafe(...)` call) — the lazy-query methods the tap's await would swallow, which is the exact assumption that makes timing the in-transaction and reserved lanes safe; (b) every return of the `sql` proxy's `apply` and `get` traps, and of the reserved-handle wrapper, that issues a statement routes through observeStatement (or runOnPool, the acquire gate wrapped around it) — a branch returning the executor's query directly is red — plus the reserve interception, its in-transaction refusal, all three lane names at a call site, and the `[db] slow query` line emitted in exactly ONE file; (c) query_tap.ts reads its arming through readEnv only (comments stripped before the process.env scan), names both armed postures, and holds no module-level mutable state (an ALS frame, so it needs no module_state_tripwire entry). Positive control per leg: the chain detector on planted offenders and on the Map `.values()` idiom it must not match, and the untapped-return detector on a planted raw executor return. Honest limit: legs (b) and (c) are lexical scans of two files, brace-balanced per trap, not a type-level proof. |
| test/unit/zzscale_corpus_native.test.ts | The museum-scale zz corpus — asserts that zzscale_corpus.ts actually carries every shape the budget gates depend on, measured through the ENGINE's doors rather than the generator that wrote it: the section resolves to matrix_test (never the installation's `matrix`) with its six components, real section_list columns and a section_map whose thesaurus.order opens getChildren's ordering branch; 1,220 records with ids contiguous from 1 and no holes; a wide node holding 440 direct children (floor 400) returned in DESCENDING id order, which is only possible if orderChildHits ran; depth exactly 3 below the root (level 4 empty) with 1,199 descendants (floor 1,000); a poly-hierarchy island whose one term is reachable from both parents, stores two parent locators with distinct id_keys and distinct per-parent order values, and is disjoint from the tree; exactly two dd96 indexation locators from one owner record, stored in a non-ascending order so a sorted answer is distinguishable from an echoed one; and a string distribution whose metacharacter coverage is checked against the REGEX_META class PARSED OUT OF src/core/search/builders/builder_string.ts (floor >10 characters), so a character added to the engine without a corpus value goes red. Teardown asserts dropZzScaleCorpus() === 0 AND that the trigger-derived matrix_string_search / matrix_relation_index rows are gone, after a pre-condition assertion that they existed (floor 1,000) so the zero cannot be vacuous. A positive control plants an uncovered metacharacter in the declared class and asserts the coverage predicate reports it. Limit: this proves the corpus HAS the shapes; it does not itself bound any cost — a consuming budget gate must state its own ceiling. |
